symptom: A page variable declared `Enumeration(Mod.Enum)` is stored and described as `String`; a variable typed `Unknown` reverts to `String` on the next page rewrite
cause: Two silent defaults, stacked. `mdlTypeToBsonType` had no enumeration case and returned `DataTypes$ObjectType` for anything unrecognised; `localVarTypeToGen` then had no ObjectType case and returned a `StringType`. A type nobody had mapped came out as "String", twice, without a word
insight: The qualified name was in the AST all along — the visitor keeps the data type's raw SOURCE TEXT, so `Enumeration(Mod.Status)` arrives complete and only needed parsing; look there before adding a field. A `DataTypes$EnumerationType` needs its `Enumeration` by-name key or Mendix resolves it to null, so an enumeration with no qualified name is deliberately NOT written as one. Fix all four corners together — builder, both writers, and DESCRIBE — or the round trip loses the type at whichever end was missed; `Unchanged page …` on a describe → exec is the proof that reader and writer agree. Stacked defaults are the pattern to look for here: each one is individually defensible and together they erase information.
